signals.title: Norton goes A2, but its new 450cc bike has a few secrets, including its name
signals.summary: Norton will unveil a new 454cc, A2-compliant motorcycle at EICMA 2026. Currently known as the 450 Urban, the new model will come in two versions, with its official name still to be revealed. Norton is preparing to enter the 450cc segment with a new model line aimed at urban riders. Referred to as the Norton 450 Urban, which is a working title for now, the new bikes will make their world premiere at EICMA 2026, where their proper name is also set to be revealed. The new machines mark a significant expansion of Norton's developing range, taking the British manufacturer into a more accessible category below its existing flagship Manx and Atlas models. The new Norton 450 will be offered in two distinct styles, with the second taking its inspiration from the street tracker genre. While the standard model adopts the cleaner look of a modern naked roadster, the tracker-inspired version gets black cast wheels, a grey frame and swingarm, extended mudguards, handguards, fork protectors, a flyscreen and unique seat trim. Both share the same engine, chassis and core equipment, meaning the choice is largely about styling and the type of riding experience each design is intended to evoke. The tracker brings a flat-track influence, which will also likely affect the riding position a little. Both versions are built around a new 454cc liquid-cooled single-cylinder engine producing an A2-compliant 47PS at 8,000rpm and 45Nm (33.2lb-ft) of torque at 6,000rpm. Power is sent through a six-speed gearbox, with a quickshifter available, while a target kerb weight of under 180kg and a 12-litre fuel tank underline the bike's focus on everyday usability. Norton says the new model has been developed to offer an approachable riding experience without feeling like an entry-level motorcycle, with the company instead describing it as an entry point into the Norton brand. The aim is to combine accessible performance with the design and finish associated with its larger machines. The new 450 is based around an aluminium frame, which Norton describes as unique in its class, and paired with a 43mm fully adjustable KYB upside-down fork and a KYB rear monoshock with rebound and preload adjustment. The level of adjustment on offer does stand out in the A2 segment, with only a small number of bikes in the class gaining such adjustability. Braking comes from ByBre, with a 320mm front disc and 240mm rear disc, supported by cornering ABS. Both versions also get traction control, cruise control and three riding modes, alongside dynamic LED headlights. Other equipment includes an eight-inch TFT touchscreen, smartphone connectivity, keyless ignition, heated grips, tyre pressure monitoring and a USB-C charger. The standard version uses 17-inch cast wheels, road tyres, a silver frame and silver wheels. The more rugged-looking alternative gets black cast wheels, a grey frame and swingarm, extended mudguards, handguards, fork protectors, a flyscreen and different seat trim. Norton says both retain the same underlying performance and accessibility, with the second version adding a little more versatility beyond the tarmac. Styling takes inspiration from the company's heritage, including the 1927 Norton CS1, with the frame and swingarm forming a prominent part of the bike's visual design. Norton has also focused on details such as minimal visible fixings, covered fuel caps and engine components, aiming to give the new model a more considered finish than might be expected in this category. It’s a design theme Norton started with the Manx and Atlas models, which both feature fairing and bodywork fixings that are tucked away and cleanly out of sight. Speaking about the new bikes, Brian Gillen, Chief Technical Officer, Norton Motorcycles, said: “Norton’s Resurgence respects our 128-year history, but it is also unashamedly forward-looking. Every new Norton is being developed around the same core principles of distinctive design, engineering detail, accessible performance and technology that enhances the connection between rider and machine. EICMA 2026 shows how we are applying those principles across an increasingly broad range of motorcycles.” The 450 will be a central part of Norton's EICMA 2026 display, alongside production versions of the Manx R, Manx, Atlas and Atlas GT. The show also marks one year since the company announced its Resurgence strategy, backed by more than £200 million of investment from its parent company, TVS. For now, the 450 Urban name remains provisional. Norton says the motorcycle's official name will be announced when it makes its public debut in Milan. signals.title: Honda’s purest track-focused CBR1000RR-R Fireblade arrives in style
signals.summary: Honda has launched the new CBR1000RR-R Fireblade HRC Works Edition, which arrives littered with premium components, and MotoGP-style technology. Honda has launched its purest track-focused CBR1000RR-R Fireblade to date with the all-new HRC Works Edition. To no surprise given its full name, the HRC Works Edition takes the standard CBR1000RR-R’s spec-sheet and ramps it up quite considerably. Finished in unmistakable HRC racing colours, the Fireblade Works Edition looks every inch a factory superbike that’s ready to compete with Ducati’s all-conquering Panigale V4 R. Its iconic red, white and blue paint scheme pays homage to Honda's legendary racing heritage, while the bike also features an aggressive aerodynamic fairing, sculptured bodywork and a purposeful appearance. At the heart of the new model is the same short-stroke 1,000cc inline four-cylinder engine, producing 160kW (214.6bhp) at 14,000rpm and 114Nm (84.1lb-ft) at 10,500rpm. The bike’s peak output remains unchanged, and this is the same across all three variants of the 2027 CBR1000RR-R, which also includes the SP model. Built as the foundation for a WorldSBK race machine, the 2027 CBR1000RR-R Fireblade HRC WE shares the frame and aerodynamic upgrades with the Fireblade SP, however, it introduces a range of competition-focused enhancements. Starting with adjustable steering-head and swingarm-pivot geometry, the HRC WE also gains Öhlins mechanical race suspension and Brembo Hypure Sports front brake calipers. Specifically, suspension is handled by NPX28-30 USD front forks and a TTX36 rear shock, while stopping power comes via Brembo Hypure Sports four-piston radial-mount front calipers, which Honda claim to save 32g compared to the previous Stylema design. Additionally, a single-seat configuration and CFRP (Carbon Fibre Reinforced Polymer) dual-element wing structure, alongside front mudguard and rear seat ducts, and an optional MotoGP-style HRC bottom-neutral shift pattern complete the bike’s setup. The added benefit of the CFRP dual-element winglets is that they generate significantly higher aerodynamic load than the previous design. Meanwhile, the upper wing surface area is now 2.4 times larger than before, while Honda says it has optimised wing angle, area and placement to improve front-end stability during acceleration and corner exit. At 299km/h (or 185mph), the new-style winglets generate 3.5 times more downforce than the standard CBR1000RR-R Fireblade. The HRC WE makes use of CFRP at the rear of the bike, too, with the above-mentioned rear seat ducts contributing to the overall aerodynamic efficiency of the race-ready machine. Riders can choose from five levels of adjustable power with Level 1 delivering maximum engine performance. Engine Brake also provides three levels of adjustment, with Level 1 delivering the strongest engine-braking effect through the 2-Motor TBW system. From there, the HRC WE features Wheelie Control with three levels of intervention, plus the ability to turn it off, with Level 1 again allowing the greatest amount of front-wheel lift before intervention. signals.title: 2027 Fireblade revealed, with new chassis and aero updates
signals.summary: Honda's 2027 CBR1000RR-R Fireblade gets an all-new aluminium frame, revised suspension, lighter engine components and MotoGP-inspired aerodynamics. Honda is taking a different approach to developing its flagship Fireblade for 2027, with the new CBR1000RR-R shaped around the requirements of its WorldSBK race programme before the production road bike was finalised. The result is a substantial overhaul of the iconic superbike, with a new aluminium frame, revised suspension layout, lighter components and an aerodynamic package developed alongside Honda Racing Corporation (HRC). It’s with this update that Honda will be hoping to close the gap to the marauding Ducati Panigales that have dominated superbike racing for the last few seasons. Since its introduction in 1992, the Fireblade has evolved from a road-focused sports bike into a machine with an almost unmatched racing pedigree, with wins on both short circuits and at events such as the Isle of Man TT. The current generation arrived in 2020, drawing heavily on the technology of Honda's RC213V-S road bike and RC213V MotoGP racer. It received further development for 2022 and a more substantial round of engine and gearbox revisions for 2024. For 2027, Honda says it has reversed its traditional development process. Rather than creating a road bike and subsequently adapting it for racing, its R&D engineers worked with the HRC WorldSBK team to establish the requirements of the competition machine first. The production Fireblade was then developed around those needs, with improvements targeted at corner entry, mid-corner control and acceleration on corner exit. At the centre of the changes is an all-new aluminium frame, constructed using Honda's Gravity Die Casting process and designed with a revised rigidity balance. Lateral stiffness has been reduced by 20 per cent, to improve cornering performance, grip feel and stability on both road and track. The frame works with a redesigned aluminium swingarm, which is 200g lighter than before and has a revised rigidity balance to complement the new chassis. The swingarm's lower rigidity is intended to improve rear-tyre feedback, while a move from a 525 to a 520 drive chain saves a further 270g. Honda has also altered the steering geometry and weight distribution, shifting more load towards the front wheel. The wheelbase remains 1,455mm, while rake and trail are now 24 degrees and 101mm respectively. The crankshaft centreline has been raised by 5.2mm, and seat height increases from 831.5mm to 843mm, giving the rider more room to move around the bike during direction changes. Suspension is provided by fully adjustable 43mm Showa Big Piston Forks at the front and a Showa Balance Free Rear Cushion Light shock at the rear. The latter now mounts directly to the lower section of the engine, rather than the frame, as part of Honda's revised approach to chassis rigidity. New lightweight seven-spoke wheels reduce unsprung mass, while braking is handled by Nissin radial-mount four-piston front calipers and lighter 330mm discs. A six-axis IMU manages the electronic systems, including the three-level Honda Electronic Steering Damper. The Fireblade retains its short-stroke 1,000cc inline four-cylinder architecture, producing 160kW (214.6bhp) at 14,000rpm and 114Nm (84.1lb-ft) at 10,500rpm. Peak output remains unchanged, with Honda concentrating instead on improving mid-range performance and reducing the weight of the engine. A new two-stage Variable Air Funnel system is the most significant engine development. Below 11,750rpm, the longer intake funnels are used to improve intake efficiency and strengthen mid-range performance. Above that point, they switch to a shorter configuration to maintain airflow at higher engine speeds. The two-motor Throttle By Wire system has also been revised, with separate control of the throttle valves allowing finer management of acceleration and engine braking. Other changes include revised cam timing, a new cam sprocket design offering a wider range of valve timing adjustment, updated valve springs and a higher compression ratio, rising from 13.6:1 to 13.8:1. Weight has been trimmed, too, thanks to the use of magnesium engine covers, lighter crankcases and 35 aluminium fasteners replacing heavier steel items. The first gear ratio is now five per cent taller, while revised spacing between the gearbox mainshaft and countershaft gives Honda greater flexibility when selecting transmission ratios for different racing applications. As before, a compact and lightweight titanium Akrapovič exhaust is fitted as standard. The bodywork has also been completely redesigned with input from HRC and Honda's MotoGP aerodynamic development. The new fairing is claimed to generate the same downforce as the previous design, which used external winglets, but with improved aerodynamic efficiency and reduced drag. Rather than relying on conventional wing elements, the new package uses a layered mid-section and lower aerodynamic sidepods to manage airflow around the motorcycle. Honda says the changes are intended to improve stability and cornering performance, particularly during high-speed direction changes, while also improving wind protection for the rider. Other changes include a new LED headlight with integrated daytime running lights, a lighter rear light and a 16.6-litre titanium fuel tank. Removing the previous tank's external plastic cover saves a further 1.4kg. The Fireblade's electronics package is built around its six-axis IMU and revised two-motor throttle system. There are three default riding modes, with the rider able to adjust power delivery, engine braking, wheelie control and Honda Selectable Torque Control (HSTC). Power has five adjustment levels, engine braking has three, while wheelie control offers three levels of intervention plus an off setting. signals.title: Honda launches new ADV125 adventure scooter for 2027, with 240-mile potential
signals.summary: Honda's new 2027 ADV125 brings rugged adventure scooter styling to the A1 class, with a 12.3bhp engine, long-travel suspension, TFT display and 385km claimed range. Honda is expanding its adventure scooter family for 2027 with the arrival of the ADV125, a new entry-level model that brings the rugged styling and practical approach of its larger ADV350 and X-ADV stablemates to the 125cc class. The ADV concept began in 2017 with the arrival of the X-ADV, which combined the convenience of a scooter with the styling and riding position of an adventure motorcycle. The ADV350 followed, offering a more accessible price and performance point. The new ADV125 brings the formula down to A1 licence level, offering a more rugged alternative to the conventional urban scooter. As with its bigger siblings, the ADV125 is designed primarily for road use, but Honda has given it the appearance and hardware to deal with less-than-perfect surfaces, handy for a pothole-riddled commute to work. Long-travel suspension, 165mm of ground clearance and block-pattern tyres are all part of the package, alongside an upright riding position intended to make it comfortable and easy to manage in town. Power comes from Honda's liquid-cooled, four-valve, single-cylinder eSP+ engine, the same basic unit used by the PCX125. It produces 9.2kW (12.3bhp) at 8,750rpm and 11.7Nm (8.6lb-ft) of torque at 6,500rpm, with fuel injection handled by a 28mm throttle body. Honda claims the ADV125 will cruise at around 56mph, with a top speed of 60mph. Fuel consumption is quoted at 47.6km/l in WMTC testing, which, combined with the 8.1-litre fuel tank, gives a potential range of approximately 240mph between fill-ups. The engine also features Honda's Idling Stop technology, which automatically shuts it down after three seconds when stationary, provided the brakes are applied. It restarts as soon as the throttle is opened, helping to reduce fuel consumption in stop-start traffic. Honda Selectable Torque Control (HSTC) is also fitted as standard, monitoring rear-wheel traction and intervening to limit wheelspin when required. The system can be switched off. The ADV125 uses a duplex steel cradle frame, with suspension travel of 116mm at the front and 103mm at the rear. The rear shocks feature external reservoirs, while ground clearance is set at 165mm, giving the scooter a little more room to deal with potholes, broken tarmac and unpaved roads than a conventional urban machine. Its 14-inch front and 13-inch rear wheels are fitted with block-pattern tubeless tyres, sized 110/80-14 and 130/70-13 respectively. Honda says the tyres have been selected to provide predictable handling and comfort on normal roads, while offering some additional ability when the surface deteriorates. Braking is handled by 240mm front and 220mm rear wavy discs, with the design intended to help clear dirt and water from the pads. The ADV125's specification includes a five-inch full-colour TFT display with Honda RoadSync smartphone connectivity, allowing access to selected functions including navigation, music control and messaging. A USB Type-C charging socket is also included, while full LED lighting and Honda SMART Key operation add to the equipment list. The windscreen can be adjusted through 75mm using a slide-lock mechanism, allowing riders to choose between increased airflow around town and greater weather protection on longer journeys. The riding position is upright, with a seat height of 780mm and a narrow seat profile intended to make it easier to get a foot down when stopped. Storage is another important part of the ADV125's appeal. There's 29 litres of space beneath the seat, enough to accommodate a full-face helmet, alongside a two-litre front glovebox. Emergency Stop Signal technology is also fitted, flashing the indicators under heavy braking to warn following traffic. Honda will offer the 27YM ADV125 in four colours: Pearl Falcon Gray, Pearl Cool White, Mat Cynos Gray Metallic and Mat Pearl Diaspro Red. A range of optional accessories will also be available, including heated grips, a security buzzer, a body cover and a rear carrier with a 40-litre Smart Top Box that integrates with the scooter's keyless system. The ADV125 brings Honda's adventure scooter styling and equipment to the A1 category, but its real appeal is likely to be as a more practical and distinctive urban commuter, with a little extra ability if and when the asphalt stops. signals.title: Honda Africa Twin gets major 2027 overhaul with four distinct models
signals.summary: Honda's 2027 Africa Twin range gets a new 1,131cc engine, more power, revised chassis and four models, including the new Enduro Sports and radar-equipped Adventure Sports SENSING RIDE. Honda has given its Africa Twin family one of its biggest updates in years, with a new 1,131cc engine, revised chassis, electronic suspension upgrades and a significant expansion of the model range for 2027. Alongside the updated standard Africa Twin and Adventure Sports, a new Enduro Sports model joins the family, while the range-topping Adventure Sports Honda SENSING RIDE introduces a suite of radar-based rider assistance technology. Almost becoming a brand within a brand, the Africa Twin name has become one of Honda's most recognisable badges. Originally introduced to European riders in the late 1980s, the name was born out of Honda's Paris-Dakar Rally success, with the XRV650 Africa Twin bringing some of that competition heritage to the road and trail. It was a formula that proved popular, combining a relatively lightweight chassis, a usable V-twin engine and the sort of versatility that made it suitable for everything from everyday riding to much longer adventures and tours. The original model eventually disappeared, but Honda revived the Africa Twin name in 2016 with the CRF1000L, effectively starting a new chapter for what has since become one of the Japanese manufacturer's most recognisable motorcycle families. More than 120,000 examples of the modern Africa Twin have been sold in Europe since its return, making it the second most popular model in the continent's 1,000cc-plus adventure segment, according to Honda. For 2027, Honda is taking the opportunity to broaden that appeal considerably with its new expanded and more diverse range. All four models share a substantially revised parallel-twin engine, producing more power and torque, along with a lighter frame and swingarm, a revised riding position and a new electronics package. The main differences come in how each motorcycle applies those foundations, with the standard Africa Twin retaining its all-round adventure remit, the Enduro Sports putting greater emphasis on off-road ability and the Adventure Sports concentrating on long-distance adventure touring. The standard Africa Twin remains the foundation of Honda's big-bore adventure bike family, and for 2027 it receives a comprehensive overhaul without losing sight of the balance between road usability and off-road capability. The biggest change is the introduction of a new 1,131cc parallel-twin engine, up from the previous 1,084cc unit. Capacity increases through a 2mm increase in bore, taking it to 94mm, while the 81.5mm stroke is retained. The compression ratio also rises from 10.5:1 to 12.1:1, with revised cylinder heads, cam timing, valve lift, pistons, connecting rods and crankshaft all contributing to the increased output. Peak power is now 87.5kW (117.3bhp) at 7,500rpm, a 16.5 per cent increase over the previous engine, while torque rises from 112Nm to 119Nm (87.8lb-ft) at 5,750rpm. Honda has also revised the intake system, with larger 52mm throttle bodies replacing the previous 46mm items. A redesigned exhaust system has also been introduced, which is intended to balance power delivery and emissions performance. The six-speed manual gearbox receives revised ratios and a new clutch to cope with the additional output, while Honda's six-speed Dual Clutch Transmission (DCT) remains available as an option. All versions of the Africa Twin retain the bike’s characteristic 270-degree crankshaft and uneven firing interval. The chassis has also been reworked, with the steel semi-double cradle frame and aluminium swingarm together shedding 1.4kg. A new fuel sub-tank positioned beneath the rider's seat helps lower the centre of gravity, with Honda taking inspiration from the NXR750 Dakar racer. The revised packaging is intended to make the Africa Twin feel more agile without compromising its stability on the road. Suspension is another significant area of development. Showa Electronically Equipped Ride Adjustment (EERA) is now standard equipment, having previously been an option, and incorporates Honda Skyhook Control. The system continuously adjusts damping according to the motorcycle's vertical and pitching movements, using information from the ECU, IMU and suspension stroke sensor. Honda says adjustments can be made in just one millisecond. The new 49mm Showa USD forks offer 220mm of travel, with 210mm at the rear through the Pro-Link system. Both figures represent a 10mm reduction over the previous arrangement, contributing to the lower centre of gravity. A new Minimum suspension setting also reduces seat height by 10mm, with the standard seat adjustable between 850mm and 870mm. Wheel sizes remain familiar, with a 21-inch front and 18-inch rear spoked combination wearing tubeless tyres. Braking comes from dual four-piston radial-mount front calipers and 310mm discs, with a 256mm rear disc. Visually, the 2027 Africa Twin adopts a more mass-forward appearance, with slimmer rear bodywork and redesigned dual LED headlights incorporating cornering lights and daytime running lights. The handlebars are narrower, higher and further forward, while the footpegs move inwards and slightly rearwards. The cockpit gets a substantial upgrade, too. A new 5.7-inch vehicle information display sits alongside a 7-inch full-colour TFT touchscreen, with a dedicated off-road display and compass. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are included, as is a lockable smartphone compartment with USB-C charging. The screen is electrically adjustable through 130mm, while heated grips, cruise control, knuckle guards and an aluminium rear carrier are standard. Kerb weight is 237kg for the manual version and 247kg for the DCT model, while fuel capacity remains 18.8 litres. Honda quotes a potential range of around 370km. signals.title: Harley-Davidson’s most affordable bike has just been revealed
signals.summary: Harley-Davidson has officially presented the new Sprint 440, which gains a single-cylinder engine producing 26bhp, a narrow profile that retains cruiser styling, and three colour options. Harley-Davidson’s highly-anticipated Sprint 440 has officially been presented by the American motorcycle maker, with pricing already confirmed, too. Described as “an invitation to experience the freedom and fun of motorcycling” by Harley, the new Sprint 440 combines a narrow profile and low seat height with plenty of modern tech. However, there’s no better place to start than the heart of the new motorcycle, with the Sprint 440 powered by a single-cylinder air/oil-cooled engine that produces 27 hp (around 26.6bhp) at 6,000rpm and 28 Ib-ft of torque at 4,000rpm. According to Harley-Davidson , the engine has been designed to minimize the bike’s overall weight, while the fuel tank features a capacity of 9 litres. Sticking with the engine, it features a single overhead camshaft and two valves (one exhaust and one intake), and its own electronic fuel injection (EFI) system which self-adjusts to maintain performance for changing conditions. The engine also comprises a long piston stroke that “delivers the sensation of satisfying, torquey performance at lower RPM for authentic Harley-Davidson character”, according to the manufacturer. Additionally, the bike’s six-speed transmission features overdrive ratios in both fifth and sixth gear in order to provide better fuel economy, while also reducing the engine’s rpm for when cruising at highway speeds. The clutch features assist-and-slip functionality to help reduce the required lever pressure. Braking is handled by a single front and rear disc system. The front brake makes use of a 320mm diameter disc and two-piston caliper, while a 240mm diameter disc and single-piston caliper are found at the rear. Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) is provided as standard equipment. The front suspension includes 43mm dual-cartridge inverted forks with 130mm of travel, while piggyback coil-over shocks are found at the rear with seven-step mechanical preload adjustment for load and rider preference. The Sprint 440 also gains lightweight cast aluminum wheels featuring a new 10-spoke design. Tech includes a coloured TFT display that’s presented in a 3.5-inch screen. The dashboard displays a digital speedometer, tachometer, odometer and trip meter, plus indicators and warning symbols. A full dose of LED lighting is also found aboard the Sprint 440. Speaking about the new motorcycle, Harley-Davidson President and Chief Executive Officer, Artie Starrs said: “The new Harley-Davidson Sprint 440 model is our invitation to ride. It’s an ideal motorcycle for a variety of riders -- the new rider who wants to build skills and confidence, but also a great option for returning riders who want to get back on the road or as an uncomplicated and fun ride for experienced riders. “The sensation of riding a motorcycle is like flying without leaving the ground, and the Harley-Davidson Sprint 440 model welcomes everyone to share in this experience.” Pricing for the Sprint 440 starts at £4,995 in the UK, but that only applies to the Dark Billiard Gray option, which is the base colour. If customers are interested in either the Vivid Black and Teal Thunder variants, then the price rises to £5,195. Still, the Sprint 440 offers a very affordable way to get started with the American brand for riders in the UK, rather than many of its large-capacity models which tend to be priced at the higher end of the market. The Harley-Davidson Sprint 440 motorcycle is making its public debut at the EICMA Motorcycle Show in Milan, Italy, which takes place on November 5-8. According to the marque, it will be available through participating Harley-Davidson dealerships globally, although launch times and availability vary by market. signals.title: ZXMoto founder breaks the most unusual motorcycle world record that still exists
signals.summary: Zhang Xue, the founder of Chinese motorcycle maker ZXMoto, has been having some fun ahead of this week’s EICMA show after setting a new Guinness World Record on two wheels. ZXMoto founder Zhang Xue has set a new Guinness World Record for the longest distance travelled on two wheels across open water. Riding a modified ZXMoto MX450 machine, Zhang set a new record of 40.74km (around 25.3 miles) in Mayang Miao autonomous county, Huaihua, Hunan province. Zhang’s new record comfortably surpassed the previous distance of 31.8km (19.7 miles), with the attempt carried out on October 25. According to reports in China, the attempt began at 11am local time with rescue boats and medical teams on standby throughout the challenge. Guinness World Record officials were also present to make sure the attempt could be validated via GPS tracking, timing data, and audiovisual records. The MX450 motorcycle was equipped with special water floatation slides underneath both tyres, as well as waterproof modifications. The astonishing part about this achievement is that it comes 17 years after Zhang's first attempt at a water ride at the age of 22. On that occasion Zhang was said to be limited by vehicle technology and design, resulting in all four attempts ending in the water, with his best distance reaching only 20 meters. It should not come as a surprise that Zhang, who also founded fellow Chinese motorcycle brand Kove and served as the company’s CEO before leaving, took part in such a challenge. Zhang is a well-known off-road enthusiast, who started Kove with five other investors in 2017. Zhang left Kove rather abruptly in 2024 before launching ZXMoto a few months later. ZXMoto’s rise has been impressive, with the Chinese company already proving to be a formidable competitor in the World Supersport championship with the 820RR-RS. signals.title: LiveWire CEO resigns as company admits financial problems are mounting
signals.summary: LiveWire is contending with huge financial issues heading into the closing stages of 2026, but Harley-Davidson might not be ready to save its electric spin-off. LiveWire might be set to unveil the new DUST Hightail motorcycle at EICMA 2026, however, the electric startup seems to have bigger issues on its hands. The Harley-Davidson -backed company released its Third Quarter Financial Results on October 29, and below all the sales and revenue figures mentioned, the brand made reference to growing concerns regarding its ability to survive going forward. It appears as though LiveWire has been in trouble for quite some time, with motorcycle sales failing to reach the intended targets. The biggest concern for LiveWire is the growing amount of debt that has amassed, which is set to mature further in 2027. Speaking about its current struggles, LiveWire said this in its report last week: “Management has determined that conditions and events raise substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the date the Company's September 30, 2026 consolidated financial statements are issued. The Company's recurring operating losses, negative cash flows from operations, limited liquidity resources, and anticipated future funding requirements contributed to this determination. “The Company continues to evaluate and pursue comprehensive financing and other strategic alternatives, which may include significant capital raises, strategic partnerships or investments, sales, and other strategic transactions, intended to support the Company's operations and execution of its business plan; however, there can be no assurance that such efforts will be successful or that any such transaction will be available on terms acceptable to the Company, our lienholders or stockholders.” This statement was provided just one week after CEO Karim Donnez resigned from his position, alongside the appointment of Roy Gallagher of the Ankura Consulting Group as the company’s new chief restructuring officer. It remains to be seen what a full restructure will look like for LiveWire, and whether this will be enough alongside numerous other changes that are needed. The company might not be able to rely on Harley-Davidson’s help either. CEO Artie Starrs spoke about LiveWire’s future during Harley-Davidson’s Q3 investor call, saying: “We don't intend to fund the operating losses of the team going forward. signals.title: From track to road: Alex Lowes changes speed with motorcycle licence training
signals.summary: Four-time WorldSBK race winner Alex Lowes has finally completed his motorcycle licence training. 2013 British Superbike champion and four-time WorldSBK race winner, Alex Lowes, has passed his motorcycle licence training test. While Lowes has been racing on the world stage since 2014, riding on the road was a completely new experience for the British rider. Organised by Derby Kawasaki , which teamed up with Shires Motorcycle Training, Lowes recently completed his CBT prior to his Module 1 and Module 2 tests. Lowes underwent his CBT training aboard a Z125 before sticking with Kawasaki machinery for his ‘big bike’ training. This is not the first time that a successful racer has waited years before undergoing their full motorcycle training. In fact, it is quite regular for racers to wait for long periods of time, while others have gone their full careers without learning how to ride on the road. Former grand prix and Isle of Man TT racer Danny Webb, aged 35, also passed his motorcycle licence training recently with Suzuki. Detailing his entire journey from the CBT training to his Mod 2 test, Lowes said: “So, I can now legally ride a motorcycle. It was a good day, I enjoyed it. I really enjoyed the Mod 2 [training] day. The weather was beautiful which helped. “Finally out on the road, it was a strange experience for me after racing bikes for all these years. To be on the road and to see all the potential hazards, even though you’re riding a bit slower was a little bit daunting. It was really beneficial for me.” A post shared by Derby Kawasaki (@derbykawasaki) Lowes, who currently rides for the factory Bimota by Kawasaki WorldSBK Team, will take part in his 14th-straight season in the championship next year. The former Suzuki, Yamaha and Kawasaki rider will once again be partnered by Axel Bassani, who has been Lowes’ teammate since 2014. signals.summary: MILAN, Italy, November 3, 2026 - Honda today presented the fully redesigned CBR1000RR-R Fireblade series, its flagship supersport motorcycle, as a 2027 model at EICMA 2026 (Milan Motorcycle Show. press days: November 3–4; public days: November 5–8), held in Milan, Italy. The CBR1000RR-R Fireblade series, Honda’s flagship supersport motorcycle range, has been developed under the concept of “Total Control for the Track,” with the aim of delivering its full potential on the racetrack. For the fully redesigned 2027 model, Honda has further pursued racing victories and the joy of riding, newly designing approximately 75% of the motorcycle’s components to further enhance its competitiveness on the track. The 2027 lineup consists of three variants: the CBR1000RR-R Fireblade (Fireblade), the CBR1000RR-R Fireblade SP (Fireblade SP), equipped with electronically controlled suspension and other features, and the newly introduced CBR1000RR-R Fireblade HRC Works Edition (HRC Works Edition). The HRC Works Edition has been newly introduced as a homologation model for the FIM *1 Superbike World Championship (WSBK). It features dedicated components, including front winglets designed to enhance aerodynamic performance and cornering capability. The model is also designed to be road-legal through compliance with the regulations of individual markets. For the 2027 model, Honda sought to combine outstanding cornering performance and chassis stability during acceleration and deceleration on the racetrack with agile handling and greater freedom of control on public roads. The newly designed aluminum twin-tube frame achieves an ideal balance of rigidity. The opening in the head pipe, which channels fresh air to the air cleaner, has been enlarged to optimize lateral rigidity. In addition, the engine cylinder hangers have been changed from the previous one-piece cast structure with integrated stiffeners to a bolt-on configuration using separate brackets. This provides greater flexibility in frame design and, together with refinements to various components, reduces lateral rigidity by 20% compared with the previous model while maintaining torsional rigidity. These changes improve cornering performance, tire contact feel, and stability under acceleration, achieving an advanced balance of handling performance on both the racetrack and public roads. Furthermore, the use of a thin-wall gravity die casting (GDC) process enables highly precise rigidity tuning, allowing the frame to be formed with a minimum wall thickness of just 2mm. By optimizing wall thickness throughout the frame, Honda has achieved a weight reduction of 440g compared with the previous model. *2 The aluminum pressed-construction swingarm has also been redesigned. The pivot shaft diameter has been reduced from 20mm to 17mm, while wall thickness and pivot width have been adjusted to optimize rigidity. By reducing lateral rigidity by 12% while maintaining torsional rigidity, the new swingarm improves rear tire contact feel during cornering. Suspension damping settings have been optimized for each variant to improve performance on the racetrack while enhancing the suspension’s ability to follow road surface irregularities during everyday riding. To further reduce vehicle weight, a titanium fuel tank has been adopted. The 2017 CBR1000RR SP and CBR1000RR SP2 also featured titanium fuel tanks, but required an outer plastic cover. Advances in titanium pressing and painting technologies have made it possible to eliminate this cover on the new model, contributing to further weight reduction. Exclusive to the Fireblade SP, the fuel tank features a hand-finished hairline treatment that leaves portions of the titanium surface exposed. This design combines weight reduction with functional beauty, creating a distinctive appearance that enhances the pride of ownership. A new Honda Flagship WING product emblem, featuring a monotone silver-and-black design, is positioned on both sides of the fuel tank. The 999cm³ liquid-cooled, four-stroke, DOHC, four-valve inline-four engine features a two-stage variable-length intake air funnel system, a first for a mass-produced Honda motorcycle. The system uses a two-piece intake funnel structure that separates vertically, varying the effective length and diameter of the intake passage according to engine speed. At engine speeds of 11,750rpm and above, the upper funnel slides upward and separates from the lower funnel. This improves power output in the low-to-mid rpm range while maintaining high-rpm performance, contributing to greater ease of use across the entire engine speed range. The existing two-motor throttle-by-wire system has also been refined. More precise electronic control enables finer adjustment of the throttle valve openings, improving throttle response during acceleration and engine braking performance during deceleration. These refinements also enable smoother transitions from deceleration to acceleration, enhancing drivability and overall ease of control. In addition to these improvements, components including the cylinder head cover have been changed from aluminum to magnesium, contributing to a weight reduction of more than 200g on the Fireblade SP. The newly introduced HRC Works Edition has been developed to further enhance competitiveness in WSBK. Designed exclusively for solo riding, it incorporates numerous dedicated components. Its carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP) *3 front winglets, front fender, and rear duct fairing improve aerodynamic performance. Combined with their lightweight construction, these components contribute to improved acceleration and cornering performance. The suspension features mechanically adjustable Öhlins NPX front forks and TTX36 rear suspension, delivering consistent damping performance and road-holding capability during racetrack riding. signals.summary: - Combining Honda’s motorcycle development expertise with the latest e-MTB technology to deliver a new riding experience - MILAN, Italy, November 3, 2026 - Honda unveiled its first high-end electric-assist mountain bike (e-MTB), the Honda RN0, at EICMA 2026 (Milan Motorcycle Show; Press days: November 3–4; Public days: November 5–8) in Milan, Italy. Developed jointly with ROTWILD, a German manufacturer of high-end e-MTBs, the Honda RN0 combines Honda’s extensive motorcycle development expertise with the latest e-MTB technologies, which continue to evolve, particularly in Europe. Weighing approximately 24kg, the lightweight Honda RN0 features a proprietary carbon monocoque frame and gull-arm swingarm. By combining a highly stable frame with an electronically controlled electric-assist drive unit, the Honda RN0 delivers the fun of riding expected of a next-generation e-MTB. It also combines high pedaling efficiency with excellent terrain-following performance, delivering outstanding riding performance across a wide range of conditions, from technical trails to long-distance rides. The concept behind the Honda RN0 is “New Terrain, Same Dream.” “New Terrain” *1 represents Honda’s first venture into the premium e-MTB market and its entry into a new field. “Same Dream” expresses Honda’s enduring commitment to expanding people’s possibilities and delivering the joy of riding, the spirit of exploration, and the excitement of taking on new challenges, regardless of changes in product categories or the environments in which its products are used. Honda began researching and developing mountain bikes in the 2000s, and in 2005, its RN01 won the overall series championship in the UCI *2 Mountain Bike Downhill World Cup. Although Honda did not subsequently introduce another mountain bike to the market, the passion for mountain biking, which was developed through its research and development activities, has been passed down. The Honda RN0 carries this legacy forward into a new model. Its name embodies two ideas: “Ride Natural,” expressing a sense of connection with nature, and “Reach New Peaks,” representing the pursuit of new heights. The Honda RN0’s most distinctive features are its proprietary carbon monocoque frame and gull-arm swingarm. An efficient structural layout extending from the head tube to the rear axle delivers high rigidity and excellent feedback from the riding surface. This allows riders to intuitively understand terrain conditions and enjoy outstanding stability and control across a variety of surfaces. The combination of the carbon monocoque frame and gull-arm swingarm provides the high rigidity characteristic of motorcycle chassis design, delivering exceptional straight-line stability. At the same time, carefully engineered flexibility allows the frame to deform slightly, improving tire contact with the ground during cornering. The Honda RN0 is available in three frame sizes—S, M, and L—to accommodate riders of different builds. The geometry of each size incorporates ROTWILD’s extensive mountain bike development expertise and is optimized for the wide range of riding conditions encountered in all-mountain riding, from steep climbs to descents. The rear suspension uses a single-pivot swingarm with a linkage system. This configuration minimizes unwanted suspension movement during pedaling while allowing the suspension to respond smoothly to impacts from the terrain, achieving an effective balance between pedaling efficiency and shock absorption. The frame features a two-tone color scheme combining Pearl Moon Ash Gray and Mat Ballistic Black Metallic. The premium finish gives the Honda RN0 a distinctive presence, even against the backdrop of natural outdoor environments. The Honda RN0 is equipped with industry-leading components. The front suspension features a FOX 36 FLOAT Factory Kashima fork with 160mm of travel, while the rear suspension uses a FOX FLOAT X Factory Kashima shock. A 2.2-inch full-color display is integrated into the top tube, providing clear information on speed, remaining range, assist mode, and other riding data. The system also supports device charging through a USB-C port. Integration with the SHIMANO app allows riders to customize the SHIMANO drive unit’s settings and lock or unlock the bike’s electronic systems. signals.title: 澎湃动力，双缸休旅踏板丨赛科龙RT450，以非凡智能系统，营造便捷出行
signals.summary: 踏板的骑行舒适度，加上双缸的澎湃动力，还是一台中排量休旅踏板？说到这我想很多摩旅发烧友已经急不可耐了，今天的主角正是赛科龙最新发布的国产首台双缸中排休旅踏板：RT450 往期内容对于这辆车的静态做了测评《车规级智能配置、仪式感拉满丨赛科龙RT450从静态感受休旅踏板的魅力所在》，今天我们就来聊聊它在实际骑行过程中的体验怎么样。 动力方面搭载398cc并列同步双缸水冷发动机，最大功率31.5KW，最大扭矩44.2N·m，发动机数值还是非常可观。NFC卡片解锁后坐上车，捏住刹车就会立刻启动，这得利于FEELFUN 非凡智能系统的「感应座垫落座解锁」，搭配摩托车传统的刹车启动，使用体验非常方便，同时带有边撑熄火。 在热车阶段可以明显感受到，发动机抖动抑制做的不错，脚踏和手把没有明显的震动感，对比同级别单缸踏板确实好太多，声浪也是连绵厚实。起步给油，油门响应及时，动力衔接顺畅，没有那种突如其来的闯动感，在城市里走走停停，不需要很刻意掌控油门，就能够轻易控车。当然他并非是一只“小绵羊”，这辆车低扭较强，再加上双缸的特性，转速随着油门的开合迅速攀升，松开油门后速度线性提升，整个流程衔接流畅，看得出来在油门与发动机的调教上下了不少功夫。 说实话，我在原地挪车的时候能够感受到RT450的分量，但真正的跑起来之后，整车的跟随性带给出乎我的意料，虽然不像城市小踏板那样灵活走位，但也不笨重；打个比喻，小踏板通勤就像：敦煌飞天壁画的仙女舞蹈，柔软灵活。RT450则是：江湖武功高手指哪打哪。 低速城市通勤时，油门响应柔和，想快速超车，一把油门就能超过去，丝毫没有迟滞感，同时车辆手把、脚踏也几乎感受不到发动机的震动。 对于休旅踏板来说，除了动力优秀骑着舒服之外，制动性能方面还得要刹得住、刹得稳，才能保障骑行的安全。RT450电控系统搭载ABS 与 TCS ，搭配前西互、后日信卡钳，在低速慢刹时，制动手感线性，但制动力又很充足，能够平顺刹停；高速急刹减速也不会打破骑行节奏，制动容易把控，在保证轮胎不抱死的情况下，稳稳地将车刹停，在此期间后尾灯爆闪，能够很好提醒后方车辆，保持安全距离。 再来看看车辆在从低速区间提速至高速时的表现，RT450的动力不是突然蹿出来的暴躁感，而是像急促的鼓点般顺势而出，得利于发动机内置平衡轴+主副平衡齿，震动被抑制得很低，即使在高速长时间骑行，也不会手麻脚震；再加上气囊可调双后减震，高速驶过颠簸路段，也没有强烈的抖动感，能够很好的过滤路面颠簸，在烂路遇到大坑洼也能撑得住。 高速需要超车时，只需轻拧油门就能轻松超越，动力随叫随到，加速能力充足，双人满载带行李也不会觉得乏力；若后方有快速车辆靠近，反光镜和仪表都会有提醒，超车溜缝既安全又放心。前15后14的轮组设定，搭配玛吉斯半热熔轮胎能够死死咬住地面，相对高速急刹也不会车身发飘、龙头乱摆，完全没有大车的笨重感；在城市弯道中车身姿态也很稳，不用刻意压低自身重心，只需要惯性就可以轻松过弯。 双摇篮高强度结构的车架刚性十足，底盘整体性强，高速行驶遇到横风，车身也不会出现明显晃动；此时可以升高电动风挡，气流被风挡疏导，减少头盔与上半身风压，搭配手把、坐垫加热，长时间骑行舒适度拉满，兼顾动力、油耗与舒适性，这也是 GT 休旅踏板的核心优势。 部分同行的极速测试甚至可以到160km/h，由于没有较好路段，没能进行实测，但从充沛的低扭和这台旗舰双缸发动机的高速延展性能够体会到，这辆大踏板确实有这个实力，再加上18L的超大油箱，结合动力调教，我个人认为续航跑个400+没有问题。 强劲的低扭、顺畅的动力衔接、全套安全智能电控配置、极易操控的车身、舒适的骑行设定再加上超大的油箱，作为一台豪华休旅大踏板完全没得说，这也是我在实际体验后的感受。如果是你是一个比较挑剔的摩旅老炮、重度配置爱好者，完全可以去线下门店试骑一圈，只有自己真正感受过，才能体会到这辆赛科龙RT450独有的巡航魅力所在。

signals.title: Norton 450 Urban, world debut at EICMA 2026
signals.summary: Norton is expanding its range with the new 450 Urban, making today its world debut. Available in two versions , the new motorbike brings the British brand’s design and build quality to the urban-focused mid-capacity segment, with a model designed for everyday commuting and trips out of town. The 454 cc single-cylinder engine delivers 47 CV at 8,000 rpm and 45 Nm of torque at 6,000 rpm. The aluminium frame, fully adjustable KYB front fork and cornering ABS complete a chassis designed to combine agility and control. The two variants share the same technical platform but differ in their styling: the road version features 17-inch wheels, whilst the more rugged-looking version adds hand guards, fork protectors, a windscreen and larger mudguards. The 450 Urban joins the Manx R and Manx sports models and the new Atlas and Atlas GT adventure-touring models, which are powered by a 585 cc parallel-twin engine. signals.title: At EICMA 2026 the new solution by Trackting and TPZ Italia
signals.summary: The first lineup of motorcycle saddles with an integrated, invisible GPS anti-theft system— born from a collaboration between Trackting and TPZ Italia—makes its debut at EICMA 2026. The new product ( on display in Hall 14, Stand E19 ) responds to an issue that remains central for motorcyclists: theft protection. The Trackting DOT system combines satellite tracking, an accelerometer, a multi-operator SIM, and a rechargeable battery lasting up to six months, automatically activating via a keychain Tag that recognizes the owner to protect their privacy. In the event of unauthorized movement, the device immediately alerts the user with a phone call and a notification, tracking the vehicle in real-time on the map to assist law enforcement. Free from electrical system connections and completely untraceable, the anti-theft device can be purchased, along with compatible handcrafted saddles, directly on the TPZ Italia online shop. © Copyright 2023 Esposizione internazionale del ciclo, motociclo, accessori S.p.A. in sigla E.I.C.M.A. S.p.A - Privacy Policy - Cookie Policy - Condizioni Generali Sede legale: Via Fabio Filzi 25/a, 20124 Milano - Pi e cf: 04145450153 N° iscrizione 04145450153 - Capitale sociale sottoscritto e versato: 100.000 euro Made by Agenzia YES S.p.A.

signals.title: Yamaha unveils the NMAX E: the next-generation electric sports scooter
signals.summary: Yamaha is showcasing its new vision for zero-emission urban mobility at EICMA with the launch of the new NMAX E. Based on the brand-new A1 EV platform, the latest addition to the Iwata-based manufacturer’s range combines the unmistakable sporty DNA of the MAX range with the most advanced electric technology , positioning itself as the equivalent of a 125 cc petrol-powered model. Powered by a 3.5 kWh lithium-ion battery (with a 5 kWh option) and the compact eAxle drive unit featuring an IPMSM motor, the NMAX E delivers a maximum power output of 7.5 kW and 33.3 Nm of torque, offering a range of up to 104 km (WMTC mode). The integrated 800 W fanless charger ensures quiet and fast recharging, including via public charging stations using the new YOU Charge service. The specification is rounded off by a newly designed chassis, a 5-inch TFT display with ‘turn-by-turn’ navigation via the Yamaha Motor On app, three riding modes, TCS and a convenient reverse function. Available from spring 2027 in Avio Blue and Platinum Silver. signals.title: LS2 revamps its technical clothing collection and expands its line of accessories
signals.summary: LS2, a Spanish brand specialising in helmets and clothing for motorcyclists, is presenting the new additions to its 2027 Collection at EICMA 2026, with updates focused on technical gear. Among the jackets, the Breakout stands out : a three-layer adventure jacket with removable thermal padding and a waterproof membrane, complemented by a ventilated vest designed to accommodate a hydration pack. For the warmer seasons, the Phoenix is introduced, featuring large mesh panels, a removable membrane and AA certification. In the off-road sector, the Gravel suit makes its debut, comprising a lightweight top and trousers, whilst the X-Terrain protective jacket can be worn on its own or as an inner layer. The collection is also expanded with three new pairs of trousers , including the Breakout, which match the jacket of the same name and feature a waterproof membrane, thermal padding and removable ventilation panels. When it comes to gloves, the Nordic range is designed for winter use with a waterproof membrane and rigid protectors, whilst the Flow range features mesh panels to aid ventilation on warmer days. There are also three new additions to the boot range: the sporty and ventilated Assault , the urban Destiny and the Lotus Flyknit trainers. Among the accessories, the Irid Dynamic Visor makes its debut: a photochromic visor capable of switching from light to dark in 0.09 seconds without batteries. Also new is the Spectrum EVO , a communication system developed with Midland, updated with voice control and app management (please, read the full news about this product in this news section). signals.title: The new Aprilia SR GT 125 gets a restyling
signals.summary: At EICMA 2026, the 2027 update of the Aprilia SR GT 125 and 200 arrives with a richer standard specification than before. The first novelty that catches the eye is the new 5-inch colour TFT instrument panel, which offers more information. The display connects to a smartphone via the Aprilia MIA unit, available as an accessory, to show pictogram navigation. A USB-C socket is also standard, but the real step up is under the seat, which can now hold a full-face helmet. The restyling is completed by new wheels and new, more practical switchgear. The adventure look is backed up by a sturdy frame, long-travel suspension, greater ground clearance and tyres with an “ all terrain” tread. The i-get engines aim for top-of-the-class performance. The 125 delivers 11 kW (about 15 PS) and 12 Nm, while the 200 reaches 13 kW (about 17.7 PS) and 16.5 Nm. What is more, for 2027 the 125 also gains a higher top speed, thanks to better calibration of the final drive. The colours are Opalescent Light, Aprilia Black and the new Boulder Grey. The Sport version recalls the liveries of Aprilia ’ s sports bikes, with Red Raceway and the new Boulder Grey and Tornado Green. signals.title: Viber Alert: new dashboards and haptic technology for motorbike safety
signals.summary: The Italian start-up returns to EICMA with patented predictive software and a seat featuring haptic feedback , developed and tested in collaboration with Federico II University of Naples. Viber Alert’s technology aims to make communication between the motorbike and the rider more immediate, reducing the need to take one’s eyes off the road. At EICMA 2026, the Italian start-up is presenting a new generation of dashboards developed with ART/MAE and a system of vibrating actuators integrated into the seat, capable of transmitting alerts relating to tyres, the engine, the electrical system and ADAS systems via haptic pulses. This innovation is accompanied by patented predictive software , which combines environmental data and information from the vehicle to calculate a dynamic risk profile and provide the rider with advance warnings. The technology underwent dynamic track testing with the University of Naples Federico II and the spin-off company RIDESense during Seaside Racing 2026. Furthermore, its integration into seats is already the subject of collaborations with Soft Italia and Corbin. signals.title: Suzuki GSX-10R, the NextGen from Hamamatsu
signals.summary: Suzuki presents the GSX-10R at EICMA 2026. This new sportbike is based on the GSX-S1000 and enters the NextGen segment, slotting one step below the GSX-R1000 in the lineup. It features all-new, sleek bodywork, with an LED headlight and aerodynamic winglets on either side. The fairing leaves part of the engine exposed, showcasing the renowned K5 unit, now in Euro 5+ configuration, delivering 152 hp and 106 Nm of torque. To make the most of the bike ’ s performance, riders can rely on a comprehensive suite of sophisticated electronic systems. These include traction control, the Lift Limiter anti-wheelie system and Roll Torque Control. The real innovation, however, is Slide Control, which helps manage rear-wheel slip. Three power modes and Launch Control are also available, along with the Engine Brake Control System. Standard equipment also includes cruise control, a speed limiter and the Brake Hold Control System, which assists the rider when pulling away on an incline. The chassis features an aluminium twin-spar frame, with the swingarm made from the same material. The rear suspension consists of a fully adjustable KYB monoshock, matched by a fully adjustable 43 mm front fork. An electronically controlled steering damper is also fitted at the front. One interesting detail is the change in rear tyre size , from the GSX-S ’ s 190/50 to a 190/55 profile. The Suzuki GSX-10R is available in three colour schemes: blue, black and red. signals.title: LIUX BIG: flax fibre makes its debut in electric mobility
signals.summary: The Spanish company Liux is unveiling the L7e microcar, with a 35 kW motor, an estimated range of 270 km and a biocomposite monocoque. Lightweight construction and efficiency are the winning cards of the Liux Big project, the new urban electric vehicle that the Spanish manufacturer is unveiling for the first time in Italy on the EICMA catwalk. The vehicle features a lightweight structure : the monocoque utilises a flax fibre-based composite, used as a reinforcing material within the matrix. This solution reduces weight by 40 per cent compared to an equivalent steel structure and cuts CO₂ emissions associated with the component by 61 per cent. The lower mass also helps to minimise the energy required for driving, with benefits for overall efficiency. Classified as an L7e , the Big measures 2.75 metres in length, weighs 648 kg and offers 240 litres of boot space. The rear-mounted motor delivers up to 35 kW (47 CV) and 140 Nm, whilst the 15 kWh and 20 kWh battery packs offer a WMTC range of 215 km and an estimated range of 270 km respectively. The specification is rounded off by independent MacPherson strut suspension and disc brakes on all four wheels. The commercial launch is scheduled for the first half of 2027. The Milan event will also offer the brand the opportunity to meet potential business partners and retail operators. signals.title: Zontes ZT853-R, the new 150 hp naked previewed at EICMA
signals.summary: Part of the Zontes range the ZT853-R, a naked motorcycle that will be positioned one step above the ZT703-R. This machine boasts an aggressive design, characterized by sharp lines , full LED lighting, integrated aerodynamic winglets, and carbon fiber elements. The engine is an 847 cc three-cylinder , capable of delivering 150 hp and 12,500 rpm with a maximum torque of 90 Nm at 9,000 rpm. Zontes claims acceleration from 0 to 100 km/h in 2.8 seconds and a top speed of 280 km/h. The electronics package includes a six-axis IMU, traction control, cornering ABS, bi-directional quickshifter, four-level adjustable anti-wheelie, launch control, ride-by-wire, and cruise control. Also brand new is the 10 kg aluminum frame, paired with a single-sided swingarm. The chassis features fully adjustable Kayaba suspension. The fork has 43 mm DLC-coated stanchions with 115 mm of travel, while the rear shock absorber offers 58 mm of travel. The braking system relies on 310 mm floating front discs with Brembo M4.30 calipers. The instrument cluster uses a horizontally oriented display, providing riding information, navigation, and a stopwatch. It also debuts the Intelligent Control System 4.0 with NFC unlocking, alongside the Zontes 2.0 app, which allows you to monitor various motorcycle parameters, from tyre pressure to vehicle location. signals.title: The LV8-branded Workshop Experience makes its debut at EICMA 2026
signals.summary: To mark its 55th anniversary, LV8 Elevate is coming to EICMA with an unprecedented exhibition concept: a space that faithfully recreates the journey a vehicle takes through a real motorbike workshop. LV8 brings the EICMA 2026 slogan to life - Always the first time. A new discovery every year - by introducing an exhibition format never before seen in the sector. For the first time visitors will be able to enjoy a genuine Workshop Experience , moving through the various operational areas: the waiting area, the service check-in for initial diagnosis and the service area where tyres are fitted and balanced, suspension maintenance is carried out, and oils and technical fluids are managed. A journey that demonstrates how motorcycle lifts, workshop furniture, modular cabinets and garage equipment can be integrated into a professional, organised and functional environment. To round off the experience, a second area will be dedicated to designing bespoke workshops and meeting the LV8 team, in an informal setting where visitors can discuss their requirements and create highly customisable solutions in terms of colours, finishes and logos. LV8 Elevate looks forward to welcoming dealers, workshops and professionals from all over the world to Hall 14, stands I46 and M49. © Copyright 2023 Esposizione internazionale del ciclo, motociclo, accessori S.p.A. in sigla E.I.C.M.A. S.p.A - Privacy Policy - Cookie Policy - Condizioni Generali Sede legale: Via Fabio Filzi 25/a, 20124 Milano - Pi e cf: 04145450153 N° iscrizione 04145450153 - Capitale sociale sottoscritto e versato: 100.000 euro Made by Agenzia YES S.p.A.

signals.title: Harley-Davidson Sprint 440, a new entry-level model in the range
signals.summary: Harley-Davidson is appealing to younger riders with the Sprint 440 , a new entry-level model in its range unveiled at EICMA. Developed with Indian manufacturer Hero MotoCorp and based on the X440 platform, the Sprint 440 features classic cruiser styling , with a teardrop-shaped fuel tank, a fastback seat and a full-LED headlight with the Harley-Davidson logo at its center. Three color options are available: Dark Billiard Gray, Vivid Black and Teal Thunder, all featuring orange graphics on the tank and the Harley Hare mascot on the side panels. Power comes from a 440 cc single-cylinder engine , air- and oil-cooled, with SOHC two-valve distribution, delivering 27 hp at 6,000 rpm and 38 Nm of torque at 4,000 rpm. The assist clutch and six-speed gearbox, with tall fifth and sixth gears, make everyday riding and highway journeys more comfortable. Claimed fuel consumption is 3.1 l/100 km, giving estimated range of around 290 km. The suspension consists of a 43 mm inverted front fork and piggyback rear shock absorbers with adjustable preload. The 671 mm seat height and 189 kg kerb weight make the bike easier to handle when stationary. Equipment includes a 3.5-inch color TFT display and a USB-C port. A wide range of accessories is available, including alternative seats, side bags, a removable windshield and a backrest. signals.title: Honda ADV125, adventure style for city commutes
signals.summary: Adventure-style scooters keep winning fans, and at EICMA 2026 Honda brings the same recipe to the 125 class with the new ADV, designed for A1 licence holders. Its lines and robust proportions recall those of the X-ADV and the ADV350 , but the newcomer is not just for show. The 165 mm of ground clearance, the long-travel suspension and the semi-knobby tyres are there to tackle potholes and rough surfaces. The seat is low, at 780 mm, while the windscreen is adjustable across five positions, with 75 mm of travel. The engine is the proven 125 cc eSP+ single-cylinder, delivering 12.5 PS (9.2 kW) and 11.7 Nm of torque. Fuel consumption is minimal: 47.6 km/l on the WMTC cycle, which with an 8.1-litre tank is worth 385 km of range. The claimed top speed is 97 km/h. Start&Stop and HSTC traction control, which can be switched off, round out the picture. The equipment also includes a 5-inch colour TFT display with Honda RoadSync, Smart Key and a USB-C socket. The 29-litre under-seat compartment can hold a full-face helmet, with a further 2 litres in the front storage compartment. Among the original accessories, the 40-litre Smart Top Box, heated grips and alarm stand out. The ADV125 comes in four colours. signals.title: Honda Africa Twin 1150, more versatile than ever
signals.summary: The Honda Africa Twin 1150 2027 makes its debut at EICMA with the most extensive update in its history, ten years after the launch of the CRF1000L. The parallel-twin engine grows to 1,131 cc , with a 94 mm bore and a 12.1:1 compression ratio, and delivers 119 hp and 119 Nm. Frame and swingarm are 1.4 kg lighter, and the new fuel tank extends partly under the seat to lower the centre of gravity. The Showa EERA suspension, for its part, integrates the Skyhook Control system. Riding Modes go from four to six, all customisable, while the instrumentation has two screens, 5.7" and 7", with wireless CarPlay and Android Auto. The handlebars and footpegs have been redesigned and define a more active riding position for the rider. The range comprises three versions, sharing engine, frame and electronics. What sets them apart, by contrast, are the front wheel, suspension, weight and fuel tank. The first is the standard Africa Twin, with a 21" front wheel, an 18.8-litre tank and a weight of 237 kg, and it is the most balanced of the three. Then there is the 245 kg Adventure Sports, which has a 19" front wheel, a 24.2-litre tank for a range of about 480 km, E-Combined ABS and, in Italy, only a manual gearbox. Its Honda Sensing Ride variant adds the DCT and two radars for adaptive cruise control, collision warnings and blind-spot detection, for a total of 256 kg. Rounding out the trio is the off-road-focused Enduro Sports , the biggest novelty of the range and the only one without the electrically adjustable windscreen with 130 mm of travel. It weighs 228 kg and has mechanical suspension with 240 and 230 mm of travel, 260 mm of ground clearance, a manual gearbox and HRC Tricolour livery. signals.title: Brembo: racing technology discovers new territories
signals.summary: From the track to the road, via the aftermarket: Brembo, the Bergamo-based group and leader in the development and production of braking systems for the automotive and motorcycle sectors, returns to EICMA 2026 (Hall 5_Stand O71) with an update to its technological offerings. Among the main innovations is the new GP4 caliper , developed in anticipation of the 2027 MotoGP season. Completely redesigned, it reduces weight by 75 grams per unit and increases rigidity by approximately 5%, while maintaining compatibility with the current system. Also making its debut is Hyction, a carbon-ceramic disc derived from the CCM-R technology used in hypercars. Already introduced on the Ducati Superleggera V4 Centenario, it will be available in the World Superbike Championship starting in 2027: it weighs 1.375 kg and offers a weight savings of 450 grams per disc, with a reduction in inertia of up to 40% compared to a steel component for street-legal superbikes. On the aftermarket front, the lineup expands with the RCS24, RCS29, and RCS34 clutch control systems , designed for cable-operated motorcycles and featuring three different mechanical lever ratios, as well as the new XTRA Signature clutch disc, designed for urban and everyday use. Also making their debut are the first Brembo braking solutions dedicated to Side-by-Side (SSV) vehicles.
